defects.title: The path-based ticket action also authorizes final-document paths
defects.body: Premise: `getDocumentUrl` accepts the caller-controlled `path` and signs every existing storage object after only an Administrator check, while the new final-document design explicitly makes the persisted issued-document ID the authorization handle and keeps `storage_path` server-only. → Path: an Administrator client invokes `getDocumentUrl("applications/{applicationId}/issued/{kind}/{uuid}.pdf")` instead of `getIssuedDocumentUrl(id)`, and receives a valid download ticket for that final document. → Verdict: final-document authorization can be bypassed through an arbitrary path rather than the issued-document ID boundary, defeating the intended namespace/metadata policy and making future role-specific controls easier to bypass. Reject `applications/*/issued/*` paths in this legacy applicant-evidence action and leave final documents reachable only through `getIssuedDocumentUrl`.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:231-251 accepts a caller-controlled path and signs any existing storage object. → Path: an Administrator invokes getDocumentUrl for applications/{applicationId}/issued/{kind}/{uuid}.pdf instead of getIssuedDocumentUrl(id). → Verdict: a final document is authorized by arbitrary path rather than its persisted issued-document ID.

app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:231-251 → getDocumentUrl accepts a path parameter, checks storage existence, and creates a download ticket without validating the path namespace or an issued-document record.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:822-831 → getIssuedDocumentUrl already resolves a persisted issued-document ID and applies current-version restrictions for Secretaria.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:300-317 → final-document storage_path is server-only and the persisted issued-document ID is the authorization handle.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:559-570 → download authorization must use document ID and reject applicant evidence.

suppressions.candidate: Download ticket is not bound to an active session when redeemed
suppressions.note: The TechSpec explicitly keeps the endpoint ticket-only and places authorization before ticket issuance; tickets are HMAC-signed and expire after 300 seconds.

suppressions.candidate: Public uploader does not inspect file contents or allowlist extensions
suppressions.note: The supplied filename is sanitized, destination category is server-allowlisted, storage resolves paths within its root, and unknown extensions are served as application/octet-stream; no concrete executable-content or path-escape flow was found.

suppressions.candidate: Observation body may contain markup supplied by Secretariat
suppressions.note: The only reviewed renderer places body in a React text node and does not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so markup is escaped rather than executed.
